I cannot believe this is getting positive reviews. It must be because it's like a meme game and no ones actually playing it. This game has the quality of like a Chinese Google Play GTA clone named "Theft City Ultra"

I have beaten the entire campaign, every mission in Party Time, and 11 rounds of Arena Mode in 2.2 hrs.

Every single level has you running around holding "E" on objects and then running to the next object to hold "E" on. The combat is incredibly easy and I never died a single time. I had to skip the first mission because it bugged out (There's conveniently a skip to Mission 2 button in the Main Menu for this very reason). Each of the environments feels like it was bought out of the Unity assets store. 

It's worth like $2 if it's ever on sale for a laugh.

After my huge disappointment and even anger with Silent Hill f, I approached Silent Hill 2 Remake with some hesitation and even doubts, but my concerns quickly disappeared.

From the very first hours, the atmosphere and gameplay completely drew me in and never let go. The gameplay reminded me of Resident Evil in some ways, and I genuinely enjoyed exploring every corner of the game and reading everything I could get my hands on. All of this, combined with the story and wonderful characters, gave me an unforgettable experience that I thoroughly enjoyed from start to finish.

This masterpiece is worth every penny. Bravo! This is how remakes should be made.

The game also features an incredible soundtrack that can truly touch your soul and stay with you long after you hear it. Silent Hill 2 Remake deserves all the huge success it has received.

Remember when a game was just a game? Apparently these devs do. 

This game is a single, complete, no nonsense game. No DLC bundles. No microtransactions, no battle passes, no live services, and no BS. Just a single game with a solid amount of content, (mostly) fair difficulty challenges, a good amount of secrets to unlock, a serviceable story, and fun gameplay. It certainly helps that Journey to the West is one of my favorite stories. Blame Dragonball Z for getting me into it. 

I only wish more games were like this.

With over 800hrs of gameplay with The Forest, having played before the island's were really opened up, the mountain area accessable, and before there was a giant hole, I must say this game has come a long way. What I find best about the gam is that the developers are always working on it, even in smaller ways. I have seen many interesting early release games get abandoned by the devs in charge of it, The Forest is not one of them. It has a steep learning curve but that is part of the fun. This game is still in development and has a way to go til it is "complete", but I have high hopes for the crew as they continue developing the game.

I'm not a fan of platform games really. I'm really NOT a fan of hard platform games. I'm also really not a fan of metroidvania style platform games. So, with that in mind, how the h*ll is this now one of my all time favourite games, ever? This game simply looks sublime. The soundtrack is a thing of beauty, so much so that the soundtrack was literally the only thing that kept me going through some of the harder parts of the game (I'm looking at you, Ginso tree escape). Then there's the story. I really wasn't expecting the emotional hits that this story has. Only the second game for me to really affect me emotionally. I genuinely love this game despite everything about my gaming preferences saying I shouldn't. I'm so looking forward to the sequel...

In The Deed you take a role of Arran Bruce, the "black sheep" of the Bruce family.

Your father, whom you were never on good terms with, intends to disinherit you, but you aren't going to let all the wealth and fortune fall in the hands of your sister (whom you were never on good terms with, either). And so you come to visit on the day of your father's 50th birthday with a vicious plan in mind. 
What plan, exactly? That's entirely up to you!

Pick one of the objects around the house to use as a weapon, plant some evidence to avoid the blame and ty to frame someone for your dirty deed. But whatever you do, do it carefully or the Inspector will find out...

PROS:
- Fast-paced "Push Forward Combat"
- Extremely fluid gameplay (over-all)
- Soundtrack is BANGING
- Quick short levels
- Lots of replayability
- Unique art style, characters and world-building
- FUN GAME - if it wasn't, the price wouldn't be worth it, and people who make fun games deserve to get paid

CONS (which can all be patched out):
- Needs an optimisation pass in the later "exterior" levels where framerate drops below 30 fps
- Some enemies can shoot through walls at corners

No wonder Devolver Digital picked this game up - it's right up their alley.

I played through the whole game on steamdeck and absolutely loved it; runs flawlessly and looks great too. The gameplay loop immediately hooked me and I really enjoyed upgrading my ship and exploring the world. The game has such a strong identity with all aspects from the art design and music to the game systems and story working in tandem to create an atmosphere that is both relaxing and creepy. The Lovecraftian/ cosmic horror themes are such a perfect match for this type of game and it can be genuinely scary at times, particularly in the early game, getting caught out at sea when night creeps in makes you feel so panicked as you try to navigate your way through the fog with your only source of light blinking out back to the nearest dock before something finds you. If you haven't played this yet it is definitely worth it and the DLCs are pretty great too. <3

Lets start with the obvious, this game is absolutely gorgeous, the level of details is simply amazing.
The atmosphere is eerie, giving you a feeling of dread and uneasiness at all times (reminding me of the Forest Temple in Ocarina of Time), way to make me feel nostalgic!

And i really commend the developers for using Scandinavian folklore as an inspiration, even for things spooky.
There's to many games with horror elements, and it's way to often random monsters, or merely amalgamations of things perserved as scary or discomforting, and it's getting tiresome at times.
So this is a fresh new take i'm all for!

I'm still mesmerized by this game, it certainly lived up hype and praises it got, and i would highly recommend it to just about everyone that feels like they're up for a grand adventure!
